summary: Teams of 2-4 secondary division students create a 3D computer animation (up to 2 minutes) visualizing a new non-profit animal shelter, including storyboard and concept art/prototype. The animation must show exterior, interior, and outdoor spaces, and demonstrate how the shelter serves animals and the community. Teams present their project live and answer judges’ questions.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes for setup
No more than ten (10) minutes for the presentation
No more than five (5) minutes for judges’ questions
Presentation will be stopped at ten (10) minutes
submission_requirements: Submit the following in one combined PDF: Clickable URL to 3D Animation, Storyboard, Concept Art/Prototype, Works Cited, BPA Release Form(s), AI Usage and Documentation Form
Upload completed projects to a video/file sharing link (Vimeo, YouTube, Dropbox, etc.)
Projects must be viewable on Windows and Mac platforms
Set the access level of your project to one of BPA’s recommended settings
Follow BPA Graphic Standards and make proper use of the BPA logo and/or organization’s name
Cite all sources on the Works Cited page
Secure a signed BPA Release Form(s) from any person whose image or work is used in the project
deadlines: National Deadline: April 1, 2027, 11:59 p.m Eastern Time
what_to_bring: Optional - Students may use one single-sided laptop, notebook, or tablet for their presentation
competencies: Utilize industry-standard editing and 3-D animation software and develop animations through storyboarding and scripting tools to ensure clear narrative structure, timing, and alignment with project objectives
Apply color grading, realistic textures, and dynamic special effects using modern digital tools to enhance visual impact, depth, and storytelling in multimedia projects
Incorporate seamless transitions, audio editing, lighting effects, and strategic placement of titles and graphics to enhance narrative flow and branding in multimedia projects
Apply audience analysis and design principles & elements to develop multimedia content that is relevant and engaging for defined target groups across platforms

rubric.criterion: Team followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

Team submitted the correct information, in the correct format, as one (1) PDF file: 1. Clickable URL to 3D Animation 2. Storyboard 3. Concept Art/Prototype 4. Works Cited 5. BPA Release Form(s) 6. AI Usage and Documentation Form

rubric.description: Predominantly original assets, creatively designed and well-integrated into the project.
Models show exceptional craftsmanship, detail, and technical skill throughout.
Camera work, timing, and transitions are dynamic, and polished, and enhance storytelling and clarity.

Strong, consistent use of multiple animation principles, resulting in a fluid, lifelike, and engaging motion throughout. Animation principles such as: Squash & Stretch, Anticipation, Slow-In/Slow-Out, and Secondary Actions are evident.
Concept art and storyboards are detailed, and creative, and clearly guide the final animation’s vision.
Animation is highly engaging, polished, and memorable. Stands out for creativity and execution.
Lighting is dynamic and effectively enhances atmosphere, focus, and storytelling throughout.
Audio is exceptionally clear, and well-mixed, and enhances mood, storytelling, and transitions.
All transitions are seamless, and polished, and support the project’s narrative flow.
The text is clean, polished, and free of grammar, spelling, and punctuation errors.

rubric.criterion: Team followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Team maintains good eye contact, use appropriate gestures and body language, and vary their tone and pace adequately.
Presentation content flows adequately, and each team member's role is clear and integrated into the presentation. Transitions between speakers and/or points are smooth.
Presentation demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and includes relevant and accurate information
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.
At least two original team members were present during the presentation.
Setup lasted no longer than three (3) minutes, and the presentation lasted no more than ten (10) minutes.

judging_notes: AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed
Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the team within the time allotted
No Internet access will be provided on-site at NLC; however, contestants may provide their own access to be used only for their presentation to the judges
Only the team captain should complete the submission
Finals may be part of the competition
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring
eligibility_notes: Any secondary division contestant may enter this judged team event
A team will consist of 2-4 contestants
Teams must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked
Entries that do not follow the provided topic or the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation Policy will be disqualified
Each state is allowed three (3) entries
